flawed_step: The claim leaves out the exception in Whitney's theorem: K3 and K_{1,3} have the same line graph but are not isomorphic.
counterexample: G1 = K3, with vertices a,b,c and edges ab, bc, ca. G2 = K_{1,3}, with center x, leaves p,q,r and edges xp, xq, xr. Both graphs are finite, simple and connected. In L(G1), each pair of edges shares an endpoint (ab and bc share b, bc and ca share c, ab and ca share a), so L(G1) = K3. In L(G2), every edge contains x, so any two edges share an endpoint and L(G2) = K3. So L(G1) is isomorphic to L(G2). But G1 has 3 vertices and G2 has 4, so G1 and G2 are not isomorphic.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The triangle K3 and the star K_{1,3} are both connected, and both have K3 as their line graph. They are not isomorphic, since one has 3 vertices and the other has 4. This is the only exception in Whitney's line graph isomorphism theorem.
